answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. The stake does not establish personhood; it makes multiplying identities costly, while random audits prevent an attacker from knowing which account will be checked. For example, atlas, nadir, and orchard can each post the same bond, but a swarm of thousands must tie up thousands of bonds and risks losing them if caught.
